briefings.headline: Brent closed its third weekly loss at $92.57, but a third night of Houthi missiles at Riyadh and another Hormuz tanker strike after the close point to upside gap risk at Monday's open, against a surplus, strong-dollar and Fed-hike backdrop.

Oil is caught between Houthi strikes on Riyadh and unverified Hormuz mine claims on one side and a global equity rout, a stronger dollar and a likely Fed hike on the other, with Brent heading for a third weekly loss.

Front-month Brent is steady near $92 as a surprise US crude and gasoline build and a hawkish Fed offset continuing Hormuz and Houthi attacks, with the Trump-Xi-Putin talks in Shenzhen the day's main swing factor.

Brent is trading near $91 as a 5.28 million barrel API crude build outweighs a new ADNOC vessel attack in Hormuz and US-Iran strikes across the Gulf, so today's EIA report and the Trump-Xi-Putin summit are the next tests.

Brent has slid to about $91.7 as surplus expectations outweigh a fresh run of Hormuz tanker attacks, so the next 24 hours turn on whether Iran's two-day reopening plan gains traction or the attacks begin to cut physical flows.
